jobs.title: Compiler Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Getting a model correct on that hardware is the frontend's job; making it fast is yours. Our hardware does not look like a CPU or GPU, so its compiler backend can't be borrowed from one. As a Compiler Engineer focused on the backend, you will help design and build the custom compilation that maps LLM inference onto it, from scheduling and memory planning to the code our hardware actually executes.

You will work at the boundary between the compiler and the hardware, closely enough to know when an optimization belongs at a different layer, or when the right answer is a new abstraction. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will measure your work against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Code Generation**: Build the passes that turn lowered programs into the code our hardware executes, designing new compilation approaches where conventional ones don't fit. Success means correct, efficient code for every operation our models need.
* **Scheduling and Memory Planning**: Own how work and data are scheduled and placed across our hardware's resources, measured by utilization and end-to-end latency on LLM inference.
* **Fusion and Dispatch**: Own fusion and dispatch decisions for LLM inference, so the hardware spends its time computing rather than moving data.
* **Hardware Co-Design**: Work the abstraction layer between the compiler and the hardware, and feed compiler constraints back to our hardware architects while the design can still change.
* **Profiling and Validation**: Validate every optimization with measured results from simulators, FPGA prototypes, and then silicon, and maintain a performance regression suite the team trusts.
* **Cross-Team Handoffs**: Take lowered programs from our frontend compiler engineers, and decide with the team which operations the compiler generates and which use hand-tuned kernels.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Deep experience with compiler optimization or code generation for accelerators or other non-CPU targets: scheduling, tiling, fusion, or resource allocation
* Comfort working close to hardware: you think in terms of memory bandwidth and utilization as well as asymptotic complexity
* Willingness to design compilation approaches from first principles when existing ones don't fit the hardware
* Track record of shipping optimizations that moved a measured performance number
* Comfort building software for hardware that is still evolving, from simulation through bring-up
* Fluency in Python, and familiarity with C, C++, or Rust

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Experience with PyTorch's compilation stack (TorchDynamo, FX, Inductor, torch.export) or other ML compilers, such as IREE, TVM, or XLA
* Experience compiling for in-memory, spatial, or other non-von-Neumann compute targets
* Background in hardware design tools such as logic synthesis or place-and-route
* Experience building or using cycle-level or performance simulators to guide optimization decisions
* Contributions to open-source compiler or kernel infrastructure (e.g., PyTorch, Triton, TVM, MLIR, LLVM)
* Publishing or presenting compiler or performance work at venues such as MLSys, ASPLOS, or CGO

***Equal Employment Opportunity Statement***

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.*

***Accessibility Accommodations***

***Privacy Notice***

==============

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

**About Ramp Labs**
-------------------

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both.

**About the Role**
------------------

Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop.

You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving.

* Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment
* Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on
* Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks
* Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship
* Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work

**What You Need**
-----------------

* Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions
* Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast
* Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise
* Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it
* Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces

* Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL)

We’re solving core problems like agent identity and delegated access, tool approval and standards around making agents aware of changes on 3rd party platforms.

As a senior engineer on this team you'll not only own our APIs, token infrastructure, authorization, SDKs, and more, but work with external companies to make it easier for developers to build agents that integrate with their products. You’ll need to balance both high uptime and fast performance with flexibility to allow for seamless connection to many systems that weren’t designed with agents in mind. If you’re looking for a role that will put you at the center of how agent identity and credentials work, this is it!

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Own and improve our infrastructure (uptime, performance, secure storage of credentials and keys) and developer experience for Connect
* Work with industry leaders within and outside of Vercel to propose and implement new authentication and authorization protocols for AI era

* Make Connect the obvious way to give an agent a credential, extending the SDKs , consent-redirect flow, and framework adapters.
* Reduce the cost of the next hundred integrations, so most new providers become configuration rather than code.
* Work directly with the teams building on Connect, and turn what you learn into platform improvements.

**About You**
-------------

* Deep, practical understanding of **OAuth 2.0/2.1, OIDC, and JWTs** — not just wiring up a client library, but reasoning about authorization codes, PKCE, refresh semantics, audience and scope restriction, token exchange, and what each of those actually protects against.
* A **security instinct for integration code specifically** — SSRF and DNS rebinding, confused-deputy and mix-up attacks, redirect-URI validation, webhook signature verification, tenant isolation. You've either found these bugs or fixed them.
* Strong **TypeScript**, and comfort developing backend and frontend components.
* Experience integrating with **many third-party APIs**, an appetite for the reality of it — undocumented behavior, non-compliant OAuth, inconsistent errors — and the judgment to absorb that mess behind a clean abstraction.

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

**About the role**

Agents are becoming first-class users of the internet. They sign in, call APIs, deploy code, and act on behalf of people and teams. That raises questions the web was never designed to answer: Who is this agent? Who does it work for? What is it allowed to do, for how long, and how do we know?

As an engineer on the [*Agent Auth and Identity*] team, you'll help answer those questions. You'll build the systems that let agents and people authenticate, delegate access, and act safely across Vercel and the services our customers connect to. This is foundational work: identity and authorization sit underneath everything we ship, and getting them right for agents will shape how modern software gets built.

The scope is intentionally broad. You might spend one quarter designing how credentials are issued and scoped for autonomous agents, and the next building the developer-facing APIs and SDKs that make secure auth feel effortless. You'll own systems end-to-end, from design through long-term operation in production.

We're looking for engineers who care deeply about security and developer experience in equal measure, enjoy working on problems without established playbooks, and want to define how trust works in an agentic world.

**What you'll do**

new_jobs.title: Robotics Research Engineer
new_jobs.description:
As a Robotics Research Engineer on our Robotics team, you'll design, train, and evaluate robotics policies from imitation learning to reinforcement learning to foundation/VLA models using Zeromatter's simulation platform, then validate, and iterate against real hardware. This work is grounded in real customer use cases as much as internal research goals. The manipulation and automation tasks you train and validate often trace directly back to a problem a customer is trying to solve. You'll work closely with our Dynamics team, who own Physics Engine development, to make sure the simulator keeps pace with what policy training needs. You'll be running the experiments, in sim and in the lab, that push our simulator's fidelity and our policies' transfer performance forward together. Responsibilities may vary from month to month, but here are some examples of things you might find yourself working on.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Design and run experiments training robotics policies (imitation learning, reinforcement learning, VLA models, etc.) entirely or primarily in simulation.
* Work hands-on with physical robots (e.g. bimanual manipulator arms) to collect real-world data, validate sim-trained policies, and characterize the sim-to-real gap.
* Collaborate with our Dynamics team to identify simulation fidelity gaps that limit transfer performance, and help prioritize and validate fixes.
* Build and maintain data pipelines and evaluation frameworks/benchmarks for policy training and transfer performance.
* Prototype new tasks and domains (e.g. dexterous manipulation, cross-embodiment transfer), often grounded in real customer use cases, to expand what Zeromatter's platform can demonstrate.
* Read, evaluate, and adapt techniques from state-of-the-art robot learning research for use on Zeromatter's platform.
* Contribute findings and results to customer-facing technical materials and demonstrations.
* Build reusable libraries and tooling (in Python, Rust, and/or C++) to support this work at scale.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* You have an engineering or related technical degree (e.g. robotics, computer science, mechanical/electrical engineering, physics) or equivalent hands-on experience.
* Experience training and evaluating robot learning policies (imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and/or foundation/VLA models) gained in industry, in a research lab, or through graduate/postdoctoral work.
* Hands-on experience working with physical robots including collecting data, running experiments, and debugging real-world hardware/software issues.
* Proficient in Python, Rust, and/or C++, with experience in ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.
* Comfortable working with incomplete information, iterating quickly between simulation and real-world validation.
* Familiarity with the practical challenges of sim-to-real transfer (e.g. domain randomization, system identification, observation/action space design, adaptation).
* Bonus: Experience with dexterous manipulation or other contact-rich manipulation tasks.
* Bonus: Experience with cross-embodiment policy learning or transfer across robot platforms.
* Bonus: Experience with teleoperation systems and data collection pipelines.
* Bonus: Experience working end-to-end across the robotics stack, including perception, classical and learned control systems, task planning, etc.
* Bonus: Familiarity with physics/dynamics simulation engines (e.g. MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or custom/proprietary engines).
* Bonus: Publication record or open-source contributions in robot learning, embodied AI, or manipulation.

We are hiring an AI Infrastructure Engineer to be the technical depth of that team. This role spans the full stack of a GPU deployment: you will install and commission the hardware, configure the Linux hosts and the InfiniBand or RoCE fabric that connects them, and own the Tier 2 and Tier 3 tickets that no one else can close. When a node fails repeatedly, you are the person who finds out why.

This is a hands-on role. You will still be in the aisle with a torque wrench during deployment windows. You will also write the runbook that prevents the next escalation, tune the fabric that shaved 8% off a customer’s job time, and sit in the vendor call explaining why their firmware is the root cause.

The work is hybrid. Deployment windows, hardware break-fix, and physical layer work happen on site. Configuration, diagnostics, ticket ownership, automation, and documentation can happen from wherever you work best.

* Perform root cause analysis on server hardware failures: correlate IPMI/BMC event logs, MCE and EDAC records, kernel messages, thermal and power telemetry, and vendor diagnostics to distinguish a genuine component failure from firmware, configuration, environmental, or workload causes.

* Identify recurring failure patterns across the fleet — a DIMM slot that fails repeatedly, a firmware revision correlated with GPU falloff, a rack with marginal airflow — and drive the systemic fix.

* Participate in a shared on-call rotation for infrastructure incidents.

* Tune and validate RoCE deployments: PFC and ECN configuration, lossless queue setup, and congestion control behavior under collective traffic.

new_jobs.title: VLA/WAM Research Engineer
new_jobs.description:
At Flexion, we're building the intelligence layer powering the next generation of humanoid robots. Our mission is to accelerate the transition from fragile prototypes to real-world humanoid deployment. We are founded by leading scientists in robot reinforcement learning (ex-Nvidia, ex-ETH Zürich), and backed by leading international VC firms. In just months, we’ve gone from our first line of code to deploying real humanoid capabilities.

### **The role**

As our VLA/WAM Research Engineer, you'll develop the foundation models that power our humanoid robots, spanning model architecture, large-scale pre-training, adaptation, and post-training.

You will work across the model lifecycle: designing VLA and World-Action Model architectures, training foundation models on large and diverse embodied datasets, developing methods for efficient adaptation to new tasks and embodiments, and using robot experience to continuously improve model capabilities.

In particular, we are looking for researchers and engineers with deep experience in one or more of the following areas: VLA/VLM or multimodal model architecture, large-scale foundation-model pre-training, world models and predictive learning, robot learning, or post-training and continual learning. If you have strong depth in one of these areas and are excited to work across the broader problem of building general-purpose robot foundation models, you will be a strong fit for the role.

### **Key responsibilities**

* VLA/WAM Architecture: Design and develop multimodal foundation models combining vision, language, robot state, actions, and temporal context for general-purpose robotic control.
* Foundation Model Pretraining: Develop and execute large-scale pretraining across diverse robot embodiments, teleoperation, egocentric human data, and simulated experience.
* Training Recipes & Scaling: Improve data mixtures, training objectives, optimization strategies, and distributed training workflows to deliver increasingly capable foundation models on a regular cadence.
* World-Action Models: Develop predictive world and action models for representation learning, future-state prediction, planning, and robot policy improvement.
* Adaptation & Mid-training: Develop methods to efficiently adapt pretrained models to new tasks, environments, embodiments, and capabilities.
* Post-training & Reinforcement Learning: Improve models using real-world and simulated robot experience, including imitation learning, RL, reward/value-guided learning, and specialist-to-generalist distillation.
* Continual Learning: Develop methods to learn from autonomous rollouts, failures, interventions, and recoveries while retaining existing capabilities and avoiding catastrophic forgetting.
* Evaluation & Research: Design rigorous experiments, evaluate models in simulation and on real robots, and use results to guide architecture and training decisions.

  
**Requirements**  

* Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with hands-on experience developing and training modern deep-learning models.
* Research or engineering experience in one or more of the following: VLA/VLM architectures, multimodal foundation models, world models, large-scale pretraining, robot learning, or RL/post-training.
* Experience owning substantial model development or training experiments, including architecture choices, training objectives, optimization, and evaluation.
* Solid understanding of modern deep-learning architectures, representation learning, and the relationship between data, training objectives, and model performance.
* Ability to design rigorous experiments, diagnose training failures, and use empirical results to guide research decisions.
* Familiarity with large-scale datasets, model training workflows, and the challenges of generalization across tasks, environments, or embodiments.
* Ability to critically evaluate recent research and translate promising ideas into working models and experiments.
* Comfortable working across model architecture, training, and adaptation while bringing particular expertise in at least one of these areas.

**Additionally, the following are a plus but not required:**

* Experience training VLA, VLM, diffusion, flow-matching, video/world models, or other multimodal generative architectures.
* Experience with distributed training, multi-node GPU systems, large-scale data mixtures, and foundation-model training optimization.
* Experience with reinforcement learning, offline RL, reward/value learning, specialist distillation, or continual learning.
* Experience with predictive world models, video generation, latent dynamics, or self-supervised representation learning.
* Experience with multi-embodiment robot learning, action representations, or adapting policies across different robot platforms.
* Experience working with teleoperation, egocentric video, simulation, autonomous rollouts, or other large-scale embodied datasets.
* Experience evaluating learned policies on real robots, particularly humanoids or dexterous manipulation systems.

new_jobs.description:
**About Ramp**
==============

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

**About Ramp Labs**
-------------------

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both.

**About the Role**
------------------

Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop.

You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment
* Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on
* Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks
* Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship
* Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work

**What You Need**
-----------------

* Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions
* Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast
* Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise
* Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it
* Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces
* Taste for what is worth measuring

**Nice-to-Have**
----------------

* Industry experience on an eval, benchmarking or post-training team
* Built RL environments or verifiers for agentic tasks
* Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL)
* Built or contributed to eval frameworks (verifiers, lm-evaluation-harness, HELM or similar)
* Familiarity with accounting, finance or other expert-domain work
* Public work we can look at: a benchmark, an eval suite, a failure-analysis write-up

Government technology has failed citizens, veterans, public servants, and service members for decades.

Kaizen powers America’s application layer. We replace the legacy systems federal agencies run on with modern software, built with craft. The ticketing platform a resident uses to visit a presidential library. The marketplace DoW uses to procure counter-drone systems to protect lives and critical infrastructure. The system a Veteran uses to access benefits. We build systems of record, of national consequence. Our AI-native modules and harness allow us to do so in weeks, not years.

You'll be one of a small number of engineers working directly on the highest-leverage features on our platform: intelligent intake flows, AI-powered case routing, constituent-facing portals that replace decade-old government interfaces.

new_jobs.title: Compiler Backend Engineer
new_jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Getting a model correct on that hardware is the frontend's job; making it fast is yours. Our hardware does not look like a CPU or GPU, so its compiler backend can't be borrowed from one. As a Compiler Engineer focused on the backend, you will help design and build the custom compilation that maps LLM inference onto it, from scheduling and memory planning to the code our hardware actually executes.

You will work at the boundary between the compiler and the hardware, closely enough to know when an optimization belongs at a different layer, or when the right answer is a new abstraction. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will measure your work against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Code Generation**: Build the passes that turn lowered programs into the code our hardware executes, designing new compilation approaches where conventional ones don't fit. Success means correct, efficient code for every operation our models need.
* **Scheduling and Memory Planning**: Own how work and data are scheduled and placed across our hardware's resources, measured by utilization and end-to-end latency on LLM inference.
* **Fusion and Dispatch**: Own fusion and dispatch decisions for LLM inference, so the hardware spends its time computing rather than moving data.
* **Hardware Co-Design**: Work the abstraction layer between the compiler and the hardware, and feed compiler constraints back to our hardware architects while the design can still change.
* **Profiling and Validation**: Validate every optimization with measured results from simulators, FPGA prototypes, and then silicon, and maintain a performance regression suite the team trusts.
* **Cross-Team Handoffs**: Take lowered programs from our frontend compiler engineers, and decide with the team which operations the compiler generates and which use hand-tuned kernels.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Deep experience with compiler optimization or code generation for accelerators or other non-CPU targets: scheduling, tiling, fusion, or resource allocation
* Comfort working close to hardware: you think in terms of memory bandwidth and utilization as well as asymptotic complexity
* Willingness to design compilation approaches from first principles when existing ones don't fit the hardware
* Track record of shipping optimizations that moved a measured performance number
* Comfort building software for hardware that is still evolving, from simulation through bring-up
* Fluency in Python, and familiarity with C, C++, or Rust

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Experience with PyTorch's compilation stack (TorchDynamo, FX, Inductor, torch.export) or other ML compilers, such as IREE, TVM, or XLA
* Experience compiling for in-memory, spatial, or other non-von-Neumann compute targets
* Background in hardware design tools such as logic synthesis or place-and-route
* Experience building or using cycle-level or performance simulators to guide optimization decisions
* Contributions to open-source compiler or kernel infrastructure (e.g., PyTorch, Triton, TVM, MLIR, LLVM)
* Publishing or presenting compiler or performance work at venues such as MLSys, ASPLOS, or CGO

***Equal Employment Opportunity Statement***

*Normal Computing is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.*

***Accessibility Accommodations***

*Normal Computing is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@normalcomputing.com.*

***Privacy Notice***

*By submitting your application, you agree that Normal Computing may collect, use, and store your personal information for employment-related purposes in accordance with our* *Applicant Privacy Notice**.*

new_jobs.description:
At R1, we’re transforming how healthcare works by combining nearly two decades of revenue cycle expertise with advanced technology, including analytics, AI, intelligent automation and workflow orchestration. We pair that technology with the irreplaceable expertise of our people to help hospitals, health systems and medical groups improve financial performance, simplify administrative complexity and create better experiences for patients and providers.

All Together Better defines our culture and the way we work. We’re a diverse, global team united by a shared mission to make healthcare work better for all. Across technology, operations and support functions, our people bring deep expertise, empathy and ingenuity to the work we do. Here, collaboration fuels progress, adaptability sparks innovation and every voice can help shape what’s next for R1 and the future of healthcare.

  

**About R37**  
R37 is R1’s AI innovation lab, building technology to transform healthcare.

  

Our flagship platform, Phare OS, uses AI and automation to improve critical pre-bill workflows, including authorization, utilization management, documentation and coding. By identifying and resolving issues before claims are submitted, Phare OS helps prevent denials, improve reimbursement and move revenue cycle work upstream.

  

What makes R37 different is the opportunity to build advanced AI at real-world scale. R1 works across 95 of the top 100 U.S. health systems, giving R37 access to the data, workflows and reach needed to make an immediate impact:

* 180M+ claims

* 550M+ patient encounters

1.2B+ workflow actions and outcomes annually  



This is startup-level ownership with enterprise-level impact. You’ll build technology that moves from idea to real healthcare environments, solving complex problems at scale and changing how healthcare works.

As our Platform Engineer, you will build shared platforms that enable 250+ engineers and AI scientists to build, ship, and operate software at scale. You will shape architecture across platform domains, solve systemic challenges, and build capabilities that improve engineering velocity, reliability, and AI deployment. To thrive in this role, you must bring deep cloud-native platform experience, strong technical judgment, and the ability to lead complex initiatives across teams.

**Here’s what you will experience working as a Platform Engineer:**

* Contributing to or leading architecture, implementation, and production operations, making sound technical decisions suited to your level of scope in complex environments
* Working on cross-functional initiatives, from well-defined projects to ambiguous, organization-wide challenges, and turning them into scalable, long-term technical solutions
* Building and growing your expertise in cloud-native platforms, infrastructure automation, containers, observability, modern software delivery practices, and production reliability
Partnering with and influencing stakeholders to improve developer experience and build secure, resilient systems at scale  

**Required Skills:**

* 2 - 7+ years of software engineering experience, including building and scaling developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, internal tooling, or shared services for large engineering organizations
* Experience contributing to or leading architecture, implementation, and production operations while making high-impact technical decisions in complex environments
* Experience navigating or driving ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives and translating organizational challenges into scalable, long-term technical solutions
* Deep expertise in cloud-native platforms, infrastructure automation, containers, observability, modern software delivery practices, and production reliability
At the Staff level, strong stakeholder leadership and influence, with experience improving developer experience and building secure, resilient systems at scale  

  

**Role Leveling:**

We are looking for candidates at various levels, ranging from Level 2 to Staff

* **L2:** Independently delivers a complete end-to-end project, owning design, implementation, and delivery of scoped work (Compensation Range for L2: $140k – $200k)

* **L3:** Leads delivery of larger projects, handling increased technical complexity and ambiguity, providing light guidance to L2s on shared work (Compensation Range for L3: $140k – $253k)

* **Senior:** Team Lead responsible for managing a portfolio of projects that contribute to major technical initiatives. (Compensation Range for Senior: $140k – $294k)

* **Staff:** Impact at the organizational level. Responsible for leading multiple teams or multiple broad initiatives simultaneously, ensuring that high-level technical goals are met across the entire organization. (Compensation Range for Staff: $140k – $350k)

  

**Benefits**

* Top-of-market compensation, including bonus that starts at 10%

* Flexible PTO

* Comprehensive health benefits

* 401(k) matching

* Inspiring, brilliant, mission-driven teammates
